To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the traffic at source-destination level can be modeled by the packet-train model and the traffic at the network level can be modeled with the long-memory model (self-similar model).
(1) the packet train model can be used for performance analysis at source destination level, and (2) the long memory model can be used at aggregate level.
the data traffic can be characterized as a superposition of packet trains and that the packet trains are self-similar.

modeling and analysis of the traffic of modern data communication networks.
modeling of the data traffic in communication networks and the analysis of the performance of the networks.
performance evaluation and modeling of modern data communication networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the traffic at different levels of aggregation has different characteristics.
data traffic at source-destination level and at the aggregate level is different and the models should be used accordingly.
the packet train models are appropriate for the traffic at source-destination level and long-memory model is appropriate for the aggregate traffic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data traffic at source destination pair level can be modeled as packet trains, while at aggregate level the data traffic can be modeled as long-memory process.
the packet train models can be used to describe the source traffic at a source-destination level and the long-memory models can be used for the aggregate traffic at the network level.
the packet train models are suitable at the source destination level and the long-memory model is suitable for aggregate traffic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to consider the characteristics of traffic at the source destination level to model the traffic at aggregate level.
the traffic at the source destination level is not self-similar and it does not follow the heavy tailed distribution.
the traffic at source and destination level is not the same as at the aggregate level.
